items.response:
I only have the winter schedule: the indoor Leslieville Farmers' Market runs Sundays 10:00-14:00 at Jimmie Simpson Rec Centre until Apr 26 2026, with no Saturday winter market. I don't have the date the summer market starts back up, so I'd rather check than guess.
Action: Look up the market's outdoor season start date and hours, and tell you.

Have a great dinner. The Kitsilano pool is open tomorrow 7:00-20:45, with lanes closed until 9:00 for swim club, so go after 9. Since Leo's swim shirt didn't make the trip, a regular T-shirt and sunscreen will do for the day.
Action: Nothing needed tonight.

Posting the beta retro reminder to #payouts-launch now. Here is the table (fee = rate x amount + fixed fee):

| Plan | Rate | $100 payment | $1,000 payment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | 2.9% + 30c | $3.20 | $29.30 |
| Growth | 2.6% + 25c | $2.85 | $26.25 |
| Scale | 2.2% + 20c | $2.40 | $22.20 |
| Enterprise | custom | n/a | n/a |
Action: Post the retro reminder to #payouts-launch and confirm once it's up.

Scheduled for 9:00. For Priya, questions that cut through: is Toronto a step up (bigger projects, a path to partner) or a sideways move, and who would she work for there? What does she lose in Montreal (friends, partner, lease, French daily life), and is there a cost to saying no? Could she try it first with a 3-month secondment, and which city does she picture herself in five years out? Toronto has plenty of old buildings and is bikeable, which suits her.
Action: Schedule the Slack message for 9:00 tomorrow and put Priya's questions in a note you can forward.

I'd make a chocolate yogurt loaf with sprinkles: one bowl, Leo can measure, stir and add the sprinkles, and it's in the oven 50 minutes later. While it bakes he can make a paper 'Happy New Year' topper, and it tastes better after a few hours, so Wednesday morning is perfect. Stores close at 18:00 on Wed 31 Dec, so get ingredients earlier.
Action: Save the recipe to your notes, add the ingredients to the shopping list, and start a list of weekend-morning baking projects for January.

Draft: 'Hi neighbours! Street yard sale this Sat 4 Oct, 9 am to 1 pm (rain date: Sun 5 Oct). Please set up tables on your own driveways, and no early birds before 9, please!'
Action: Save it as a draft and post it to the group chat when you say go.

I'd tell Marcus to put numbers on both: the extra 10% in after-tax dollars against about 35 minutes saved each way, roughly 70 minutes a day and around 6 hours a week. Then compare what money doesn't show: caseload, mentorship, hours and a path to grow. If the raise is only a few thousand after tax, the short commute usually wins.
Action: Draft a short text for you to send Marcus.

Merry belated Christmas! Pyjamas at 11, a Lego truck on its third build and Sam asleep on the couch with Biscuit is peak boxing day. Hope it stays this slow.
Action: Nothing needed, enjoy the day.

Try this one: 'Why do accountants make terrible comedians? Their punchlines always have to be reconciled by Friday.' Clean, finance-themed, and no crypto.
Action: Save it to your notes for Friday's standup.

I don't have your street's yard waste schedule saved, so I won't guess dates. I'll look up the City of Toronto collection calendar for your address and add the next two pickups with a reminder the evening before.
Action: Look up the yard waste schedule for your address, add the next two pickups to the calendar, and ask you for the address if it isn't on file.

I don't have your lesson day or time, or your latest notes from Carlos, in front of me. A good default for the week is to review the mistakes from your last lesson, do 15 minutes of speaking practice, and drill new vocabulary from the current topic.
Action: Find the class on your calendar, block two 30-minute study slots before it, and ask you which topics tripped you up last time.

That sounds like a perfect porch morning, enjoy the coffee and sun. I'll push the career day prep to later.
Action: Snooze the career day prep reminder until later today.

I don't see a confirmation yet. Note that Dr. Lin moved in March 2026 to Danforth Smiles, 822 Danforth Ave near Pape station (416-555-0144), so I'll look for confirmations from them, not from the old Queen East Dental.
Action: Search your email and calendar for November confirmations from Danforth Smiles for you and Leo, and if there's nothing, contact them to confirm.

Yes, it used to be January. The league's longer season moved it later: the 2002 game slid into February after the 9/11 postponement, and the move to a 17-game schedule in 2021 locked it into the second Sunday of February. Sunday is the TV choice, since it's the biggest audience of the week.
Action: None.

Tell him the siren sounds to the dog like another dog howling, so he's singing back to say 'I hear you!' Dogs have super hearing, and howling is how they talk to each other from far away.
Action: None.

I don't have anything saved from that browsing, so I'll search rather than guess. I'll check your notes, email, photos and saved links for the backsplash or wall inspiration, and if nothing turns up, pull a fresh shortlist so you can answer Nate before Monday.
Action: Search your notes, email and photos for the wall inspiration, and build a fresh shortlist if I find nothing.

Here's a draft for Priya: 'Hi [client name], thanks for the updated direction on the facade. Because this is the second change to the brief since the design was approved, the revised drawings fall outside our original scope. We'd be glad to take them on under a short change order covering the additional hours, which I'll send over, and once it's signed we can start right away.'
Action: Send Priya the draft, with [client name] and the hours estimate left for her to fill in.

No, damage deposits aren't allowed in Ontario. Under the Residential Tenancies Act a landlord can only take a last month's rent deposit, and for real damage beyond normal wear and tear they must apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board themselves and can't just deduct it. Scuffed walls are often normal wear. If Diego paid a separate damage deposit, he can ask for it back and file a T1 application with the LTB within a year of moving out.
Action: None.

Both set: a reminder to send Tom your comments on the strategy memo by Friday, and one to pick up Leo's library books from the Pape branch on Saturday morning. I don't have the branch's Saturday hours, so I'll check them so the reminder lands at the right time.
Action: Create the Friday reminder for Tom's memo comments, check the Pape branch's Saturday opening hours, and set the Saturday-morning pickup reminder.

You're welcome. Two things are still waiting: the two holds at Pape/Danforth are ready until Sat 25 Apr, and Tom still needs the link to the beta merchant numbers before his exec sync tomorrow morning.
Action: Keep Tom's request flagged for after dinner.

Ha, that's a great question, and it deserves a very serious answer. Hope you can put your feet up soon. The T-Rex costume arrives Tue 27 Jan.
Action: Nothing needed.

I don't have today's Canada Post estimate, but regular international letter mail to India usually takes a couple of weeks or more, so I'd send it early. For your mom's address in Bandra, I'll use what's in your contacts.
Action: Look up Canada Post's current delivery estimate from Toronto to Mumbai and tell you the latest date to mail the card.

Wen Li handles data requests through #data-requests, and she needs at least three business days of notice and a written metric definition, otherwise she bounces them. So it needs to go in as soon as possible to land before Wednesday. The Payouts Health dashboard shows failed-payout reasons, but I'm not sure it splits by receiving bank.
Action: Draft the #data-requests post for your OK: failed payouts by receiving bank, count and rate, last 30 days, needed for Wednesday's roadmap prep, with the metric definition written out.

Here's a simple Saturday: skate the Rideau Canal Skateway in the morning, with a BeaverTail snack on the ice, then lunch back at Grace and Daniel's. In the afternoon, see the ice sculptures in Confederation Park and the snow slides at Jacques-Cartier Park in Gatineau, then an early dinner so Leo's in bed on time.
Action: Save it to your notes as 'Winterlude Saturday idea' and check the 2027 Winterlude dates once they are announced.

Booking a 25-minute onboarding design review with Aisha and Diego on Thursday 26 Nov at 10:00. Agenda: 1) KYC retry screens, 2) empty states, 3) open questions.
Action: Check all three calendars for Thu 26 Nov at 10:00, send the invite with the agenda, and flag any conflict instead of double booking.

Welcome back, glad the drive was fine. After travel, a Tuesday feels like a Thursday, so I'll keep today light and flag only what's urgent.
Action: Check your inbox and calendar for anything urgent today and send you a short heads-up.

You made it to Friday. One item is still open: the talk title for the Toronto Fintech Meetup is due 18 Sep.
Action: Nothing else needed tonight.

I'll text Hannah that we'd love to come for pancakes on Sunday at 9. Since she has some night shifts, I'll text rather than call. I'll add it to the 'Okafor-Malhotra family' calendar after checking for conflicts.
Action: Text Hannah yes, check Sunday 9:00 for conflicts, and add 'Pancakes at Hannah's' to the family calendar.

I can't give you an honest grade yet, since I have no lesson log or sample of your speaking to base it on.
- Calendar rule saved: no meetings before 9:30 or after 17:00.
- To assess your Spanish, send me a short voice note or your last lesson notes.
Action: Save the calendar rule and check it against anything already booked.

Added Grace's 68th birthday on Thu 19 Nov 2026 to the calendar, with a gift reminder two weeks ahead on Thu 5 Nov. Since you're at Grace and Daniel's in Ottawa Fri 13 to Sun 15 Nov, the gift should be in hand by Fri 13 Nov.
Action: Create the birthday event, set the 5 Nov gift reminder, and add a note that the gift needs to come with you on the 13th.

From what I can see: the out-of-office for Fri 22 May is drafted (back Mon 25 May, Aisha covering payouts), and the retro RSVPs are in, with 9 accepted, Olivia tentative and Jonah not replied. The Miro board has 14 stickies so far, and the top theme is webhook retries.
Action: Check today's full activity log before I list anything else.

Three days late is fine for a silly-mug tradition. I'll search for absurd novelty mugs, ranked by ridiculousness and reviews, and check which ones can get to Vancouver in about 3 days or less.
Action: Run the search and delivery check, then show you the top few with prices and delivery times so you can pick.

For Halloween you still need to sort: the costume (tell me what he's going as and I'll make a parts list), the evening logistics (who's walking with him and when you head out), and safety gear like reflective tape, a flashlight and a pillowcase. Add treats for the door if you're giving them out.
Action: Check your calendar for Halloween night, and build the parts list once you tell me the costume idea.

I'll unsubscribe you from Wayfair, Uber Eats promos, Lululemon and Dyson, and archive their existing promo mail. Old Navy is one of the three senders that needed a login, and those are saved in Notes under Inbox cleanup, so I'll handle that one separately. I'll leave Uber receipts and other transactional mail alone.
Action: Unsubscribe from the four senders, archive their promo mail, and for Old Navy open the saved login note and ask you to sign in or confirm.

I'll skip anything scented, since Sam gets migraines from strong fragrances. For drywall dust and old curry I'd go with unscented activated charcoal odour absorbers, plus open windows, bowls of baking soda overnight and a wet wipe-down of dusty surfaces.
Action: Find in-stock unscented charcoal absorbers that can arrive before the week starts and show you the pick before I buy.

From what I can see, nothing is still running: the Big Apple hours check finished (open 8:00-20:00 on Thanksgiving Monday, 13 Oct). The only open item is waiting on you: Leo's piano on Monday at 16:30, cancel or keep?
Action: Check the full task list for anything else active and report back.

I'll pull every open payouts ticket from Linear and group them by workstream. For December launch risk, I'll flag tickets that are blocked, unassigned, overdue or have no estimate, and anything with dependencies on outside teams.
Action: Query Linear for open payouts tickets, group by workstream, and send the list with at-risk items called out and the reason for each.

Pulling your open Linear tickets tagged payouts-ga, titles and status only.
Action: Query Linear for open tickets with the payouts-ga label and list them as ID, title, status.

Booking a 25-minute call with Olivia and Aisha on the 9th at 3:30 pm, with your three-point agenda in the invite: 1) where certification stands, 2) what sales can and can't say, 3) next checkpoint. I'll word the title as GA target wording, since nothing gets shared with sales as a date until Aisha signs off.
Action: Check all three calendars for the 9th at 3:30 pm, send the invite for 15:30 to 15:55 Toronto time with the agenda, and flag any conflict.

I don't have last night's result in front of me and I'd rather not guess a score.
Action: Look up last night's Raptors final score and send you a one-line answer for Sam.

I'll find a half-hour window on the 13th in the afternoon that works for you, Diego and Aisha. Following your rule, the meeting is 25 minutes inside that window, with an agenda in the invite: 1) walk through the new onboarding flows, 2) open design questions, 3) decisions and next steps.
Action: Check all three calendars for the afternoon of the 13th, send the 25-minute invite with the agenda, and flag any conflict.

I don't have your travel dates in front of me, so I won't guess when you're arriving. I'll check your calendar and email for the booked trip before answering her. I'll also check the current local time where she is, so you know whether it's too late to call.
Action: Find your trip dates, check the local time and the usual weather for those dates, and draft a reply to your mom.

EFT is a batch bank-to-bank transfer: cheap, typically 1-3 business days, and can be reversed within return windows. A wire is a same-day, high-value transfer, costs more, and is effectively final once sent. Suggested wording for the decks: 'EFT: batch bank transfer, 1-3 business days. Wire: same-day high-value transfer, final once sent.'
Action: Put those definitions in a short note you can drop into the decks.

Anytime. The 7:50 car-move reminder is set, and the street-cleaning schedule lookup for your block is still running.
Action: None.

I don't have the earlier Ottawa flight search saved here, so I'll dig back through your email and our earlier chats for it, and if I can't find it I'll rerun it for Sam's February PD day. I'll also open your podcast note and suggest new commute picks based on what you like.
Action: Find the Ottawa flight options and send them to Sam for comparison, then read your podcast note and send a short list of new podcasts.
